learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 2 times as fast and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Baseline 300 K typical speed 508 m/s in text, rounded 510 on visual bar. At 600 K text 719 and visual 720 with 1.41 times. At 1200 K text 1016. Home reached 150 K and 359; restored 600 K before reveal.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 1.4 times, used visited 600 and 1200 K cases, and explained energy grows with speed squared, giving square root of two for doubled kelvins.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Pink moving particles above speed bar with 300 K baseline and dashed two-times marker. Rounded numbers agreed with precise text to displayed precision. Reveal text fit below controls.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Defines kelvin before asking a clear ratio prediction.
prediction.evidence: 300 to 600 K and 2 versus 1.4 versus unchanged.

interaction.reason: Two heat presets and lower slider limit reveal nonlinear scaling.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects observed ratios with squared-speed energy.

clarity.reason: Reference marks make the speed ratio explicit.
clarity.evidence: Bar labels 1.41 times and two-times target.

transfer.reason: General scaling principle is explained with same-system contrasts only.
transfer.evidence: No fresh gas or new application attempted.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard boundary and text values observed; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Doubling absolute temperature produces a smaller speed ratio.

visualExplanation.reason: Particles give motion context while bar supplies reliable comparison.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies meaning of temperature and molecular motion.

depth.reason: Connects temperature, kinetic energy and square roots.

complexity.reason: Simple controls support a square-root scaling explanation.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish motion energy from speed and reverse a squared relation.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One temperature slider and two heat buttons.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Kelvin introduced before prediction; molecular energy introduced at reveal.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Kelvin, Celsius, m/s, multipliers and square-root notation.

whyCool: Four times the kelvins is needed to reach twice the typical speed.
caveat: Animation alone cannot quantify the speed ratio; bar and numbers carry the comparison. No fresh application was attempted.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
